author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Linux auditd 3.x records, sent through the audisp-syslog plugin or read from /var/log/audit/audit.log by rsyslog. The host forwards them as syslog to the data collector. Logins, authentications and account and group changes go to Auth; execve SYSCALL and EXECVE records go to Process; sudo commands, audit configuration changes and systemd service starts and stops go to ManagementEvent; other records stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- For Linux hosts running auditd 3.x: turn on the audisp-syslog plugin (active = yes in /etc/audit/plugins.d/syslog.conf) and forward the host's syslog to the data collector, or have rsyslog read /var/log/audit/audit.log.
- Audit rules decide what is logged, for example -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k exec for program executions.

Field mapping:
- Logins and authentications (USER_LOGIN, USER_AUTH) and account and group changes (ADD_USER, DEL_USER, USER_MGMT, ADD_GROUP, DEL_GROUP, GRP_MGMT, USER_CHAUTHTOK, GRP_CHAUTHTOK) go to Auth.
- execve SYSCALL records (the process, parent, program and user) and EXECVE records (the command line) go to Process.
- sudo commands (USER_CMD), audit configuration changes (CONFIG_CHANGE) and systemd service starts and stops go to ManagementEvent.
- Other records, such as PATH, PROCTITLE and AVC, stay generic.
- Each syslog line is one record: the records of one event share the audit ID (seconds, milliseconds and serial), which the parser keeps as sensor_event_id, so join SYSCALL and EXECVE on it.
- The parser reads RAW and ENRICHED log formats, with or without node=, and takes user names from the enriched fields when present.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the record formats of the linux-audit project's field dictionary and test data.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15 (230 of 230 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and each child also passed as a separate parser under its parent.
- In Run Test the engine also keeps sensor_event_id on lines that stay generic, a field the emulator's generic schema leaves out.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines.

Known gaps:
- auditd hex-encodes values with spaces or special characters: the parser decodes the sudo command, but other encoded values, such as an EXECVE argument with a space, stay hex.
- The interpret option of audisp-syslog drops the audit ID and isn't supported.
